alt.en: A narrow newspaper column of small type: an editor's note of two paragraphs quoting the line "Calm on the listening ear of night.", then the heading "CHRISTMAS CAROLS." over five stanzas of eight lines beginning "It came upon the midnight clear,", signed "E. H. S." at the foot. Faint print from the other side of the sheet shows through.
alt.es: Una columna estrecha de periódico en letra pequeña: una nota del editor de dos párrafos que cita el verso "Calm on the listening ear of night.", y después el título "CHRISTMAS CAROLS." sobre cinco estrofas de ocho versos que empiezan "It came upon the midnight clear,", firmadas "E. H. S." al pie. Se trasluce débilmente la impresión del otro lado de la hoja.

caption.en: The carol's earliest known printing, in the Christian Register of Boston on 29 December 1849, page 206: five stanzas under the title "Christmas Carols", signed only "E. H. S.", below the editor's note welcoming new verses from the writer of "Calm on the listening ear of night".
caption.es: La primera impresión conocida del villancico, en el Christian Register de Boston del 29 de diciembre de 1849, página 206: cinco estrofas con el título "Christmas Carols", firmadas solo "E. H. S.", bajo la nota del editor que celebra unos versos nuevos del autor de "Calm on the listening ear of night".

source: Christian Register (Boston: David Reed), vol. 28, no. 52, 29 December 1849, p. 206, "Christmas Carols", signed "E. H. S.", with the editor's note above it (cropped to that column section)
library: Internet Archive, Serials in Microfilm (digitized from microfilm)
callNumber: Internet Archive sim_unitarian-register-and-the-universalist-leader_christian-register_1849-12-29_28_52, image n1; microfilm reel IA1519118-07; ISSN 0503-2644
licenceEvidence: Printed Boston, 29 December 1849 (IA record: date 1849-12-29). Words by Edmund H. Sears, died 1876 (story, [^julian]); the unsigned editor's note was written in 1849 by an adult editor (John H. Morison, per the story), who would have had to live past 1955 for it to be in copyright. PD in the US (published before 1931), the EU and Israel (life plus 70). Faithful scan of a flat page. See rights.md.

alt.en: A printed music page headed "See Israel's gentle shepherd stand." and numbered 93, with "STUDY. No. 23." and "C. M." below: two vocal staves and a two-stave accompaniment in 6/4 time with one flat, the first verse under the notes, a short closing phrase at the lower left, and stanzas 2, 3 and 4 printed at the lower right, signed "Doddridge."
alt.es: Una página de música impresa con el encabezado "See Israel's gentle shepherd stand." y el número 93, y debajo "STUDY. No. 23." y "C. M.": dos pentagramas de voces y un acompañamiento en dos pentagramas, en compás de 6/4 con un bemol, la primera estrofa bajo las notas, una frase final breve abajo a la izquierda y las estrofas 2, 3 y 4 impresas abajo a la derecha, firmadas "Doddridge."

caption.en: Study No. 23 in Richard Storrs Willis's Church Chorals and Choir Studies (New York, 1850), page 93: a setting of Philip Doddridge's "See Israel's gentle shepherd stand" that holds roughly the first half of the melody now called CAROL.
caption.es: El Study No. 23 de Church Chorals and Choir Studies de Richard Storrs Willis (Nueva York, 1850), página 93: una versión musical de "See Israel's gentle shepherd stand", de Philip Doddridge, que contiene más o menos la primera mitad de la melodía que hoy llamamos CAROL.

source: R. Storrs Willis, Church Chorals and Choir Studies (New York: Clark, Austin & Smith, 1850), Study No. 23, "See Israel's gentle shepherd stand", p. 93
library: Princeton Theological Seminary Library (digitized by the Internet Archive)
callNumber: Internet Archive churchchoralscho00will, image n98; OCLC 1041812932
licenceEvidence: Published New York 1850 (title page: "New York; Clark, Austin, & Smith, 205 Broadway. 1850."). Music by Richard Storrs Willis, died 1900; words by Philip Doddridge, died 1751. PD in the US (before 1931), the EU and Israel (life plus 70). Faithful scan of a flat page. See rights.md.
credit: Princeton Theological Seminary Library, via the Internet Archive

alt.en: A printed hymn-book page numbered 66 and headed "CHRIST.", with "CAROL. C. M." and "Richard Storrs Willis. (1819)" above four systems of music in 6/8 time with two flats, the first verse, "It came up-on the mid-night clear", under the notes. Below, hymn 158, "Christmas Carol", prints stanzas 2 to 5 in two columns, signed "Rev. Edmund Hamilton Sears. (1810) 1850." A few pencil marks are in the margin.
alt.es: Una página impresa de un himnario con el número 66 y el encabezado "CHRIST.", con "CAROL. C. M." y "Richard Storrs Willis. (1819)" sobre cuatro sistemas de música en compás de 6/8 con dos bemoles, y la primera estrofa, "It came up-on the mid-night clear", bajo las notas. Debajo, el himno 158, "Christmas Carol", trae las estrofas 2 a 5 en dos columnas, firmadas "Rev. Edmund Hamilton Sears. (1810) 1850." Hay algunas marcas a lápiz en el margen.

caption.en: No. 158 in Hymns and Songs of Praise (New York, 1874), page 66: the earliest known printing of Sears's words with Willis's tune, here named CAROL, set in 6/8 and B-flat with all five stanzas, the words dated 1850.
caption.es: El n.º 158 de Hymns and Songs of Praise (Nueva York, 1874), página 66: la primera impresión conocida de la letra de Sears con la melodía de Willis, aquí llamada CAROL, en 6/8 y en Si bemol, con las cinco estrofas y la letra fechada en 1850.

source: Hymns and Songs of Praise for Public and Social Worship, edited by Roswell D. Hitchcock, Zachary Eddy and Philip Schaff (New York: Anson D. F. Randolph, 1874), No. 158, "Christmas Carol", tune CAROL, p. 66
library: Princeton Theological Seminary Library (digitized by the Internet Archive)
callNumber: Internet Archive hymnssongsofpr00hitc, image n73; OCLC 1046530224
licenceEvidence: Published New York 1874 (copyright page: "Entered according to Act of Congress in the year 1874, by Anson D. F. Randolph & Company"). Words by Sears, died 1876; tune by Willis, died 1900; the editors were adults working in 1874, so none can have lived past 1955. PD in the US (before 1931), the EU and Israel (life plus 70). Faithful scan of a flat page. See rights.md.
credit: Princeton Theological Seminary Library, via the Internet Archive

alt.en: A printed hymn-book page numbered 63 and headed "CHRISTMAS.": two systems of four-part music ending "A-men.", marked "A little slower.", then hymn 82 with the line "I heard the voice of many Angels. Rev. v. 11." and four stanzas beginning "It came upon the midnight clear", the last beginning "O Prince of Peace, Thou knowest well", with dynamic marks such as pp and mf in the margin.
alt.es: Una página impresa de un himnario con el número 63 y el encabezado "CHRISTMAS.": dos sistemas de música a cuatro voces que terminan en "A-men.", con la indicación "A little slower.", y después el himno 82 con la línea "I heard the voice of many Angels. Rev. v. 11." y cuatro estrofas que empiezan "It came upon the midnight clear", la última "O Prince of Peace, Thou knowest well", con indicaciones de matiz como pp y mf en el margen.

caption.en: Page 63 of Church Hymns with Tunes (London, 1874), edited by Arthur Sullivan: the close of NOEL, the traditional air he rearranged, and the words as No. 82, with "The words of peace they bring" in the third stanza, a new fourth stanza to the "Prince of Peace", and no fifth.
caption.es: La página 63 de Church Hymns with Tunes (Londres, 1874), editado por Arthur Sullivan: el final de NOEL, la melodía tradicional que él rearregló, y la letra como n.º 82, con "The words of peace they bring" en la tercera estrofa, una cuarta estrofa nueva dirigida al "Prince of Peace" y sin la quinta.

source: Church Hymns with Tunes, edited by Arthur Sullivan (London: S.P.C.K., preface dated Easter 1874), No. 82, tune NOEL (begun on p. 62), p. 63
library: Princeton Theological Seminary Library (digitized by the Internet Archive)
callNumber: Internet Archive churchhymns00soci, image n86; OCLC 1041784965
licenceEvidence: Published London by the S.P.C.K., 1874 (IA record: date 1874; story: preface dated Easter 1874, early Great Queen Street imprint). Music editor Arthur Sullivan died 1900; Sears died 1876; the reviser of the words is unnamed (anonymous, published 1874). PD in the US (before 1931), the UK/EU and Israel.
